title: Design a URL Shortener (TinyURL / Bitly)
relevance: High — the classic first "design X" HLD question at campus + FAANG / Indian product cos; tests estimation, unique ID generation, Base62, read-heavy caching, and 301 vs 302.
company_notes: Extremely common campus/intern/new-grad HLD warm-up or full round at Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Meta, Uber, Atlassian, Flipkart, etc.; still asked at 1–4 YOE with deeper probes on multi-region ID allocation, 301/302 + CDN, cache stampedes, and abuse; among the most frequent HLD design questions.

phases.goal: Lock core shorten/redirect FRs, optional features, NFRs, and scale clarifications before designing.

must_hit.point: Core FRs: shorten a long URL into a short URL, and open the short URL to redirect to the long URL.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States write = create short link and read = redirect as the only required flows.

must_hit.point: NFRs: unique codes, redirect p99 ≪ 100 ms, high availability when a mapping exists, durable mappings, and a read-heavy workload.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names uniqueness, sub-100 ms redirect latency, availability, durability, and read-heavy traffic.

must_hit.point: Ask about optional FRs: custom alias, TTL/expiry, click analytics, user accounts, and delete/update destination.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly clarifies which optional product features are in or out of scope.

must_hit.point: Clarify expected URLs/day, retention (e.g. 5–10 years), custom aliases, analytics, and multi-region needs.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Asks scale, retention, alias, analytics, and geo questions before estimating.

probes: What functional and non-functional requirements are you assuming, and which optional features are in scope?

hints.1: Separate must-have create/redirect from nice-to-haves like aliases and analytics.
hints.2: State uniqueness, redirect latency, availability, durability, and that traffic is read-heavy.
hints.3: Core: shorten + redirect; NFR: unique codes, p99 ≪ 100 ms, HA if mapping exists; ask URLs/day, 5–10 year retention, aliases, analytics, multi-region.

phases.goal: Derive write/read QPS, storage growth, and short-code length from stated assumptions.

must_hit.point: Example load: 100M new URLs / month ≈ 40 writes/s average, with peak about 2–5×.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses ~100M/month → ~40 writes/s and calls out 2–5× peak.

must_hit.point: At 100:1 reads, average redirects are ~4k redirects/s, with peak tens of thousands.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Applies 100:1 read:write to get ~4k redirects/s and higher peaks.

must_hit.point: Record ~500 B → 100M/mo ≈ 50 GB/mo raw storage before retention and replication.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Multiplies ~500 B per record by 100M/month to ~50 GB/mo.

must_hit.point: Base62 alphabet yields 62^n codes; 62^7 ≈ 3.5×10^12, so interview default short-code length is usually n = 7 from lifetime URL count.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Chooses n so 62^n covers lifetime URLs and lands on length 7 with the 62^7 figure.

probes: Walk through your back-of-envelope: writes/s, reads/s, storage, and why the short code is length 7.

hints.1: State assumptions out loud for new URLs per month and read:write ratio.
hints.2: Convert 100M/month to ~40 writes/s, apply 100:1 reads to ~4k redirects/s, then size storage and code space.
hints.3: 100M URLs/mo → ~40 w/s; 100:1 → ~4k redirects/s; ~500 B → ~50 GB/mo; need 62^n ≥ lifetime URLs → usually n = 7 (62^7 ≈ 3.5×10^12).

phases.goal: Define create and redirect HTTP contracts, status codes, and optional below-the-line endpoints.

must_hit.point: POST /urls (or /api/v1/shorten) accepts long_url with optional custom_alias and expires_at, returns short_url like https://short.ly/{code}.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows a create endpoint with body fields and a short_url response.

must_hit.point: GET /{code} returns 302 (or 301) with Location set to the long URL; 404 if unknown; 410 if expired.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names redirect with Location plus 404/410 for missing/expired codes.

must_hit.point: Optional DELETE /urls/{code} and GET /urls/{code}/stats stay below the line unless analytics/delete were scoped in.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Treats delete and stats as optional, only if requirements included them.

probes: What APIs would you expose for shortening and redirecting, including status codes?

hints.1: You need one write API and one redirect read API.
hints.2: Create returns a short_url; redirect uses Location with 302/301, 404, or 410.
hints.3: POST /urls {long_url, custom_alias?, expires_at?} → {short_url}; GET /{code} → 302 Location, 404 unknown, 410 expired.

phases.goal: Model the short_code → long_url mapping and keep analytics off the redirect path.

must_hit.point: Primary table url_mapping keyed by short_code (PK, VARCHAR(8) Base62) storing long_url, optional user_id, created_at, expires_at, and is_custom.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes short_code PK with long_url and the listed optional columns.

must_hit.point: Index/PK on short_code so redirect lookup is O(log n)/O(1).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly puts PK/index on short_code for fast redirect reads.

must_hit.point: Optional reverse index or hash of long_url only if dedup of identical long URLs is required; analytics/click tables live elsewhere, not on the redirect critical path.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates optional long_url reverse lookup and says clicks are not on the hot path.

probes: What does your schema look like for the mapping, and what is indexed for redirect?

hints.1: The primary key of the design is short_code → long_url.
hints.2: Include created_at/expires_at/user_id/custom flags and keep analytics tables separate.
hints.3: url_mapping(short_code PK VARCHAR(8), long_url, user_id, created_at, expires_at, is_custom); optional long_url hash if dedup; clicks elsewhere.

phases.goal: Sketch LB, split write vs redirect services, ID gen + Base62, cache-aside, and async analytics.

must_hit.point: Client → LB/API Gateway splits into a write service (ID gen → Base62 → DB) and a redirect service (cache → DB on miss → 302 Location).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws separate write and redirect paths behind a load balancer/gateway.

must_hit.point: Cache-aside on redirect: Redis/Memcached holds hot code → long_url; miss loads from DB and populates cache.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes cache-aside for the redirect hot path.

must_hit.point: Click events go async via a queue to an analytics store so analytics never blocks redirect; scale redirect fleet much larger than write fleet on stateful-less app servers.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Enqueues clicks and sizes redirect servers >> write servers.

must_hit.point: Postgres/MySQL with PK on short_code is enough at interview scale; Cassandra/Dynamo only if pushed on massive write/partition needs; CDN/edge optional for viral codes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Starts with SQL + PK, mentions NoSQL only under scale pressure, CDN as optional.

probes: Draw the high-level architecture for create and redirect, including cache and analytics.

hints.1: Optimize the read/redirect path first — traffic is read-heavy.
hints.2: Write path generates IDs; redirect path is cache-aside then DB; analytics is async.
hints.3: LB → write (counter/Snowflake/KGS → Base62 → DB) and redirect (Redis → DB miss → 302) with queue for clicks; redirect fleet >> write fleet.

phases.goal: Defend ID-generation choice, 301 vs 302, counter allocation, and custom-alias uniqueness.

must_hit.point: Hash+truncate+Base62 is deterministic/dedup-friendly but needs collision retry; prefer counter/Snowflake+Base62 (or KGS) unless the interviewer wants identical-URL dedup.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compares hash collisions/retries vs counter/Snowflake/KGS and picks based on dedup need.

must_hit.point: 301 may be cached forever by browsers (fewer origin hits, weak analytics, hard revoke); 302 (or 301 + short Cache-Control) hits origin every click — default 302 when click tracking is required.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties 301 vs 302 to caching vs analytics/revoke and defaults to 302 for tracking.

must_hit.point: Single Redis INCR is a SPOF/hot counter; range allocator or Snowflake avoids per-write global counter hits, with tradeoffs of unused ranges on crash vs clock skew.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains range/Snowflake vs central INCR and names crash/skew tradeoffs.

must_hit.point: Custom aliases need a separate namespace or reserved prefix and a strong uniqueness check on create (UNIQUE/conditional write) so they never collide with auto-generated codes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Isolates alias namespace and enforces uniqueness only on write.

probes: Why this ID strategy over hash truncation, and would you use 301 or 302?

hints.1: Interviewers usually probe ID generation and redirect status code next.
hints.2: Contrast hash collisions vs counter/Snowflake coordination, then link 301/302 to analytics.
hints.3: Prefer counter/Snowflake/KGS+Base62 unless dedup; choose 302 for click tracking; ranges beat single INCR; aliases get UNIQUE and a separate namespace.

phases.goal: Scale redirect QPS, DB, ID generation, writes, expiry, and failure modes.

must_hit.point: Redirect QPS is dominated by cache hit rate: Redis cluster, local LRU for ultra-hot keys, CDN for viral links, and singleflight to prevent stampede on expiry.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names cache hit rate plus cluster/LRU/CDN/singleflight for hot redirects.

must_hit.point: Shard by short_code hash only if storage/QPS exceeds one primary; use read replicas for rare cache-miss storms; pre-allocate ID ranges (or Snowflake for multi-region writes).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defers sharding, adds replicas for miss storms, and pre-allocates IDs.

must_hit.point: Writes stay low vs reads: rate-limit creates, validate URLs; expiry via cache TTL ≤ expires_at plus sweeper or lazy 410 on read.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rate-limits creates and describes TTL/sweeper/lazy 410 for expiry.

must_hit.point: If cache is down, degrade to DB with shedding; if DB primary is down, fail creates but serve redirects from replicas/cache.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives concrete degrade paths for cache-down and primary-down.

probes: Where does this system break first under viral traffic, and how do you scale past it?

hints.1: Reads need cache/CDN long before the primary write DB is the bottleneck.
hints.2: Talk cache hit rate, then DB sharding/replicas, then ID range allocation and failure degrade.
hints.3: Cache cluster + LRU/CDN/singleflight; shard short_code only when needed; range/Snowflake IDs; rate-limit writes; cache-down→DB with shedding; primary-down→fail creates, serve redirects from replicas/cache.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Hash is deterministic and dedup-friendly but truncation forces uniqueness checks and collision retries; counter/range, Snowflake, or pre-generated KGS are collision-free (or pool-managed) and preferred at interview scale unless identical long-URL dedup is required — mention XOR/permutation if sequential enumerable codes are a concern.

301 lets browsers cache forever, cutting origin load but weakening analytics and making revoke/update hard; 302 (or 301 with short Cache-Control) sends every click to the origin so you can count clicks and control expiry/updates — default to 302 when click tracking matters.

tradeoffs.topic: Single Redis INCR vs range allocator / Snowflake
tradeoffs.strong_answer: A single INCR is simple but a SPOF and hot counter; range allocators give app servers batches (unused ranges lost on crash); Snowflake removes the central counter SPOF and is time-sortable but brings clock-skew concerns — range/Snowflake is the expected mid-level answer for multi-writer ID gen.

tradeoffs.topic: Same short code vs new code for the same long URL
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Product choice: hash/dedup reuses one code for identical long URLs; always-new codes suit campaigns that need distinct links and separate analytics.
Redirects can use an AP-friendly store or SQL replicas once a mapping is written; custom-alias uniqueness still needs a strong uniqueness check on create.

gotchas.trap: Putting analytics writes on the redirect hot path
gotchas.correction: Enqueue click events asynchronously (Kafka/queue) to an analytics store; never block redirect on analytics; losing some click events is usually OK.

gotchas.trap: Using UUID directly in the short URL
gotchas.correction: UUIDs are too long and defeat shortening; encode a compact ID (e.g. Base62 of a counter/Snowflake ID) instead.

gotchas.trap: Sequential codes that are easy to enumerate
gotchas.correction: Randomize/permute IDs, use longer codes, auth sensitive targets, and rate-limit redirects — short links are often public by design.

gotchas.trap: Custom alias race / taken alias without a uniqueness guarantee
gotchas.correction: Enforce DB UNIQUE constraint (or conditional write in NoSQL) and return retry/error; keep aliases in a separate namespace or reserved prefix so they never eat auto-generated codes.

gotchas.trap: Drawing Redis but skipping TTL, eviction, and hot-key stampede
gotchas.correction: Interviewers expect cache TTL (≤ expires_at), eviction/LRU behavior, and stampede control (e.g. singleflight) on the redirect path.

gotchas.trap: Preferring naive hash truncation without defending collisions
gotchas.correction: At interview scale prefer counter/Snowflake/KGS unless dedup is required; hash truncation forces DB uniqueness checks and retries.
